title: Fission Raises $10 Million for Tokenized Fund Liquidity
description: Fission closed a $10 million Series A led by Pantera Capital to expand liquidity capacity for eligible investors in supported tokenized funds.
why_it_matters: The financing targets a persistent market-structure gap: tokenized fund interests can settle digitally while investors may still face conventional redemption constraints.
keyTakeaways: Pantera Capital led Fission's $10 million Series A, with Circle Ventures and other investors participating.
Fission says eligible holders of supported tokenized funds can access capital without waiting for conventional redemption cycles.
The company plans to expand liquidity capacity, asset coverage and institutional integrations.
body: Fission announced on October 15 that it closed a $10 million Series A led by Pantera Capital. Participants included Circle Ventures, New Form, gumi Cryptos Capital, Borderless Capital and GTS chief executive Ari Rubenstein. The company provides liquidity infrastructure for supported tokenized fund products, allowing eligible holders to access capital without waiting for conventional fund redemption cycles. Fission says its platform is designed for institutional and permissioned markets, including investor-eligibility, transfer-restriction and compliance controls. The new funding is intended to expand liquidity capacity, supported asset coverage and institutional integrations. Fission also reported processing millions of dollars in transactions, but did not disclose an exact amount, valuation or expansion timetable.

facts.claim: Fission closed a $10 million Series A financing round.
Pantera Capital led the round with several named participants.
Eligible holders can access capital before traditional fund redemption cycles.
Fission designed its platform for institutional and permissioned markets.
The funding will support broader asset coverage and liquidity capacity.
